key_insight: Large Transformer language models still suffer plasticity loss, and scaling only delays it rather than fully preventing it.
engineering_relevance: For continual and long-running LLM training, model size alone is not enough; training pipelines need explicit mechanisms to preserve adaptability over time.
method: Trained GPT-style Transformer models from 5M to 314M non-embedding parameters
Used a multilingual continual learning setup
Evaluated plasticity with a held-out Vietnamese probing task and compared against stationary multilingual training
evidence_signal: The abstract reports deterioration on the Vietnamese probe across all model sizes studied, with the onset of plasticity loss following a sublinear scaling law.
watch_item: Results are based on one multilingual probing task, so the measured onset and severity of plasticity loss may depend on the evaluation choice and training regime.
paper_title: Can Scale Save Us From Plasticity Loss in Large Language Models?
